title: MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors
title_zh: MiRL：面向纠错终端智能体不当行为的目标导向强化学习

paragraphs.en: Error-targeted learning gives a legible way to improve a model: identify specific weaknesses of the model, train the model to fix these weaknesses, and check whether the weaknesses are fixed. We study how to apply error-targeted learning to terminal agents, which solve long-horizon tasks specified in natural language by interacting with a command shell. Existing error-targeted methods are designed for single-turn tasks, and existing analyses of agent failures are used to evaluate and debug agents rather than to train them. We propose Mi sbehavior-driven RL (MiRL), which first profiles the errors of a policy to find generalizable misbehaviors : kinds of wrong steps that recur across many environments. MiRL then trains the policy with RL, starting rollouts at the steps where these misbehaviors occur and rewarding a rollout only if it passes the tests and avoids the misbehavior. On Qwen3.5-4B, eight misbehaviors account for 52.1% of wrong steps. After training with MiRL, the policy repeats the measured misbehaviors 43% to 57% less often on average on unseen prefixes. MiRL outperforms TMax-4B on Terminal-Bench Lite (51.8% vs. 47.4%) and matches it on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (21.3% vs. 20.6%), while using 35% of its rollouts. These results show that error-targeted learning can be applied to realistic, long-horizon terminal tasks. 1 1 1 Project page: github.com/runchu-tian/MiRL

paragraphs.en: Error-targeted learning finds the errors a model makes and trains the model to stop making those errors ( Khan et al., 2025 ; Lee et al., 2024 ) . This approach is desirable because it makes model improvement easy to understand, as each training example is tied to some named error, and after training we can check whether that error becomes less frequent. For LLM agents, prior work has built taxonomies of agent errors ( Cemri et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2026b ) and methods that locate the step at which an agent fails ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ) . These analyses are mostly used to evaluate and debug agents, not to decide what the agent trains on. Terminal agents ( Bin et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) are typically instead trained by scaling the number of training environments ( Pi et al., 2026 ; Gandhi et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Ivison et al., 2026 ) ; for example, one TMax training run samples from 14.6K environments and takes two to three days on eight H100 nodes ( Ivison et al., 2026 ) . To our knowledge, error-targeted learning has not been applied to terminal agents.
paragraphs.zh: 以错误为目标的学习会找出模型所犯的错误，并训练模型不再犯这些错误（Khan et al., 2025；Lee et al., 2024）。 这种方法之所以可取，是因为它使模型的改进易于理解：每个训练样本都对应某个明确的命名错误，训练之后我们可以检查该错误是否变得更少发生。 对于大语言模型智能体，已有研究构建了智能体错误的分类体系（Cemri et al., 2025；Zhu et al., 2026b），以及定位智能体在哪个步骤失败的方法（Zhang et al., 2025；Zhang et al., 2026b）。 这些分析大多用于评估和调试智能体，而不是用于决定智能体的训练内容。 终端智能体（Bin et al., 2026；Liu et al., 2026）通常转而通过扩大训练环境的数量来进行训练（Pi et al., 2026；Gandhi et al., 2026；Wu et al., 2026；Ivison et al., 2026）；例如，一次 TMax 训练运行从 14.6K 个环境中采样，并在 8 个 H100 节点上耗费两到三天时间（Ivison et al., 2026）。 据我们所知，以错误为目标的学习尚未被应用于终端智能体。

paragraphs.en: Applying error-targeted learning to terminal agents is not straightforward. Existing error-targeted methods work on and are designed for single-turn problems: when the model answers a problem incorrectly, these methods generate similar problems for training. A terminal agent takes dozens of steps per task, and a failed task is often caused by one or two wrong steps, such as reporting that the tests pass without running them. This creates two difficulties. First, many wrong steps are specific to one task, so fixing them one at a time does not help on other tasks; training should instead target generalizable misbehaviors , kinds of wrong steps that recur across many tasks. Second, training from the start of a task spends most rollouts on steps the agent already performs correctly, and the agent may never reach the state where the misbehavior occurred. We therefore ask: (1) how can we identify the generalizable misbehaviors of a terminal agent, and (2) how can we train the agent directly at the steps where they occur?
paragraphs.zh: 将错误定向学习应用于终端智能体并非易事。 现有的错误定向方法针对且仅适用于单轮问题：当模型答错一道题时，这些方法会生成类似的题目用于训练。 而终端智能体每个任务要执行数十步，任务失败往往由一两个错误步骤造成，例如没有运行测试就报告测试通过。 这带来了两个困难。 第一，许多错误步骤是特定于单个任务的，逐一修复它们对其他任务没有帮助；训练应当转而针对可泛化的不良行为，即在许多任务中反复出现的那类错误步骤。 第二，从任务一开始进行训练会把大部分 rollout 花在智能体已经能正确执行的步骤上，而智能体可能永远无法到达发生不良行为的状态。 因此我们提出两个问题：(1) 如何识别终端智能体的可泛化不良行为，(2) 如何直接在它们发生的步骤上对智能体进行训练？

paragraphs.en: We answer these questions by connecting two tools: step-level error analysis of agent trajectories and RL from intermediate states. To answer the first question, we run error analysis on the policy we are about to train, which we call error profiling (Figure 1 (a)). We roll out the policy on 2,017 environments from TMax’s environment set ( Ivison et al., 2026 ) ; an error localizer flags wrong steps, a teacher model corrects each flagged step so that the rollout can continue and reveal later errors, and an annotator model groups the wrong steps into error types. Eight error types, such as “Makes false claims about tests” and “Fails to produce runnable commands”, cover 52.1% of all wrong steps and appear in 75.4% of the environments; we treat these as the generalizable misbehaviors to target. To answer the second question, we introduce MiRL, a misbehavior-driven RL recipe (Figure 1 (b)). MiRL builds on two known techniques, starting rollouts from intermediate states ( Xi et al., 2024 ; Yi et al., 2026 ) and providing reward signals beyond the binary verifier outcome ( Lightman et al., 2024 ; Gunjal et al., 2026 ) , each guided by the error profiling outputs. Each group of rollouts starts at a misbehavior prefix, the part of a trajectory just before a misbehavior step, and a rollout receives reward only if it passes the tests and a behavior judge confirms that it avoids the misbehavior of that prefix. To start from a prefix, MiRL restores the container by rerunning the prefix’s commands in a fresh container and keeps the prefix only if every command returns the recorded output.
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过结合两种工具来回答这些问题：智能体轨迹的步骤级错误分析，以及基于中间状态的强化学习（RL）。 为回答第一个问题，我们对即将训练的策略进行错误分析，我们称之为错误画像（图 1 (a)）。 我们在 TMax 的环境集中的 2,017 个环境上对策略进行 rollout；一个错误定位器标记错误步骤，一个教师模型纠正每个被标记的步骤以使 rollout 得以继续并暴露后续错误，一个标注模型则将错误步骤归入不同错误类型。 八种错误类型，例如「对测试做出虚假陈述」和「无法生成可运行的命令」，覆盖了全部错误步骤的 52.1%，并出现在 75.4% 的环境中；我们将这些视为需要针对的可泛化的不当行为。 为回答第二个问题，我们提出 MiRL，一种由不当行为驱动的强化学习方案（图 1 (b)）。 MiRL 建立在两种已知技术之上，即从中间状态开始 rollout（Xi et al., 2024；Yi et al., 2026）以及提供超越二元验证器结果的奖励信号（Lightman et al., 2024；Gunjal et al., 2026），两者均以错误画像的输出为指导。 每组 rollout 从一个不当行为前缀开始，即轨迹中不当行为步骤之前的部分，并且只有当 rollout 通过测试且行为判定器确认其避免了该前缀的不当行为时，才会获得奖励。 为从前缀开始，MiRL 通过在一个全新容器中重新运行前缀的命令来恢复容器，并且只有当每条命令都返回记录的输出时才保留该前缀。

paragraphs.en: We train Qwen3.5-4B ( Qwen Team, 2026a ) with MiRL using TMax’s RL recipe and evaluate on Terminal-Bench Lite ( OpenThoughts-Agent team et al., 2026 ) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 ( Merrill et al., 2026 ) . On held-out prefixes, MiRL reduces the rate of the measured misbehaviors by 43% to 57% on average, measured by two behavior judges. MiRL also improves task performance: with the same number of training environments (189), MiRL outperforms TMax-189 (the TMax recipe trained on the same number of environments), PivotRL ( Yi et al., 2026 ) , and a form of RaR ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) enhanced with outcome rewards (RaR+), by at least 4.2 points on Terminal-Bench Lite and 2.2 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1. MiRL also outperforms TMax-4B, the released checkpoint trained with the full TMax recipe, which samples from 14.6K environments, on Terminal-Bench Lite (51.8% vs. 47.4%) and matches it on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (21.3% vs. 20.6%), while using 35% of its rollouts. paragraphs.en: Recent terminal agents improve mainly by scaling training data. Synthesis pipelines generate terminal environments from seed tasks and taxonomies ( Gandhi et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2026a ; Pi et al., 2026 ; Ivison et al., 2026 ) or derive them from repositories and human-validated sources ( Wu et al., 2026 ; Shen et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026b ) . Some works train on tens of thousands of terminal environments or hundreds of thousands of trajectories ( Li et al., 2026b ; Pi et al., 2026 ) . Recent works improve data efficiency: Terminal-Lego ( Yang et al., 2026 ) builds a more compact dataset around the inspect-act-verify loop, and Terminal-World ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) derives 5.7K terminal environments from agent skills. Such a trend is also observed in other domains, e.g., RL for math reasoning can be effective with about a thousand or even a single carefully selected example ( Li et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) . These works improve data efficiency by improving the quality of tasks and trajectories, or by selecting learnable examples, whereas MiRL does so by targeting the general, recurring errors of the policy ( generalizable misbehaviors ).

paragraphs.en: An outcome reward scores a whole trajectory by its final state. This gives coarse credit assignment because correct steps in a failed trajectory are penalized, and error steps in a successful trajectory are reinforced. To give more specific learning signals, one line of work starts rollouts from intermediate states. R 3 ( Xi et al., 2024 ) starts RL from intermediate states of correct demonstrations and moves the start point backward as a curriculum. PivotRL ( Yi et al., 2026 ) samples several actions at each step of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) trajectories and trains only on the steps where these actions get different rewards. An action is rewarded if it is equivalent to the action in the SFT trajectory. Another line adds supervision beyond the task outcome: process reward models score each intermediate step ( Lightman et al., 2024 ) , GiGPO ( Feng et al., 2025 ) assigns step-level credit across rollouts that revisit the same state, and RaR ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) scores whole trajectories against task-specific rubrics. Compared to the second line, MiRL shapes rewards so that a rollout must avoid a specific misbehavior to be reinforced.

paragraphs.en: We aim to apply error-targeted learning to terminal agents. Our intuition is that a few general errors account for many of the agent’s error steps, so fixing these errors may improve the agent on many environments. To identify these errors, we run error profiling, as shown in Figure 3 : we roll out the policy on a pool of environments, check and record the error steps, and group them into error types. We call the types that recur across many environments generalizable misbehaviors. To train the policy at the steps where these misbehaviors occur, we propose MiRL, our RL recipe, which starts rollouts from misbehavior prefixes instead of from scratch, and adds a behavior reward to the outcome reward, so a rollout gains reward only if it passes the tests and a behavior judge confirms that it avoids the misbehavior.
paragraphs.zh: 我们旨在将错误定向学习应用于终端智能体。 我们的直觉是，少数几种通用错误造成了智能体的大量错误步骤，因此修复这些错误可能会在许多环境上提升智能体的表现。 为了识别这些错误，我们进行错误剖析，如图 3 所示：我们在一组环境上对策略进行 rollout，检查并记录错误步骤，并将它们归入错误类型。 我们把在许多环境中反复出现的类型称为可泛化的不当行为。 为了在这些不当行为发生的步骤上训练策略，我们提出 MiRL，即我们的强化学习方案：它从不当行为前缀而非从零开始进行 rollout，并在结果奖励之外增加一个行为奖励，使得一次 rollout 只有在通过测试且行为判定器确认其避免了不当行为时才能获得奖励。

paragraphs.en: A terminal environment consists of an instruction that states a user requirement, a container in which the agent runs shell commands, and a test suite that checks the final state of the container (Figure 2 ). An agent, a language-model policy π \pi , solves a task over multiple steps. Before each step, it reads the prefix , which includes the instruction, its earlier steps, and their outputs. It then takes one step: a short reasoning followed by a shell command. The sequence of steps and their outputs forms a trajectory, which ends when the agent submits or reaches a step limit. The test suite then checks the final state of the container, giving an outcome reward r o r_{o} of 1 if all tests pass and 0 otherwise.
paragraphs.zh: 一个终端环境由三部分组成：说明用户需求的指令、智能体在其中运行 shell 命令的容器，以及检查容器最终状态的测试套件（图 2）。 智能体是语言模型策略 π，通过多个步骤解决任务。 在每一步之前，它会读取前缀，其中包含指令、它之前的步骤及其输出。 然后它执行一步：先进行简短的推理，接着给出一条 shell 命令。 各步骤及其输出构成的序列形成一条轨迹，当智能体提交或达到步数上限时，轨迹结束。 随后测试套件检查容器的最终状态，如果所有测试通过则给出结果奖励 r_o 为 1，否则为 0。

paragraphs.en: Besides the policy, error profiling calls LLMs to play three roles: an error localizer that checks whether a step is problematic given its prefix, a teacher that corrects a problematic step, and an annotator that proposes error types and labels each error step with them.

paragraphs.en: To locate the errors of the policy, we roll it out on a pool of environments and let the teacher replace each error step with a corrected one, so that the rollout can reveal later errors.
paragraphs.zh: 为了定位策略中的错误，我们在一组环境上对其进行 rollout，并让教师将每个错误步骤替换为修正后的步骤，从而使 rollout 能够暴露后续的错误。

paragraphs.en: At each step of a rollout, error profiling goes through four stages, as in Figure 3 (a). (1) The policy proposes its next step from the current prefix. (2) The error localizer checks the step with its prefix, flags it only if it is likely to lead to failure, and writes a short explanation. (3) For a flagged step, the teacher writes a correction from the same prefix, so that the rollout can continue without being pushed into incorrect states. The correction is checked in the same way as a step of the policy. (4) The accepted step, either the policy’s own step or a correction from the teacher, is executed, and the rollout returns to (1) for the next step. If the teacher fails to give a correction that passes this check within three tries, the rollout is discarded. During this process, each error step is recorded with its prefix and the error localizer’s explanation.
paragraphs.zh: 在 rollout 的每一步中，错误剖析会经历四个阶段，如图 3 (a) 所示。 (1) 策略从当前前缀中提出其下一步。 (2) 错误定位器结合前缀检查该步骤，仅在其可能导致失败时才将其标记，并写出简短的解释。 (3) 对于被标记的步骤，教师从相同的前缀写出修正，使 rollout 能够继续进行而不被推入错误状态。 修正的检查方式与策略的步骤相同。 (4) 被接受的步骤（无论是策略自身的步骤还是教师的修正）将被执行，然后 rollout 回到 (1) 进行下一步。 如果教师在三次尝试内未能给出通过此检查的修正，该 rollout 将被丢弃。 在此过程中，每个错误步骤都会连同其前缀和错误定位器的解释一起被记录下来。

paragraphs.en: To find the errors that recur across environments, we group the error steps into error types, as in Figure 3 (b). We repeat this on several batches and keep the types that recur across batches. This gives a fixed set of error types. The annotator then labels every error step with one or more types from this set, or with none if it fits no known type. Finally, we keep the error types that cover at least a fixed share of the error steps and treat the others as a long tail of rare types.
paragraphs.zh: 为了找出在不同环境中重复出现的错误，我们将错误步骤归类为错误类型，如图3(b)所示。 首先，标注者阅读成批的错误步骤以及错误定位器的解释，并为每一批提出错误类型，为每个类型给出名称和定义。 我们在多个批次上重复这一过程，并保留在各批次间重复出现的类型。 这样就得到了一组固定的错误类型。 标注者随后用该类型集合中的一个或多个类型为每个错误步骤打标签，如果某个步骤不属于任何已知类型，则不作标注。 最后，我们保留覆盖至少固定比例错误步骤的错误类型，并将其余的视为由罕见类型构成的长尾。

paragraphs.en: Standard RL recipes used for terminal agent training, such as GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) and DPPO ( Qi et al., 2026 ) , start every rollout anew, from step zero. An important characteristic of these methods is that they are on-policy, that is, they train on rollouts generated by the policy itself. Starting rollouts anew would mean that we could not correct a specific misbehavior in an on-policy manner unless the identical misbehavior occurred and was detected in a fresh rollout. The highly stochastic nature of long-horizon terminal agent trajectories means that generating rollouts that display a particular misbehavior would be very compute-intensive. To fix the misbehaviors in a more targeted and efficient manner, MiRL instead starts each group of rollouts from a pre-existing trajectory prefix where the policy exhibited a misbehavior. The policy then continues from the prefix until the rollout ends. We select a fixed number of misbehavior prefixes for each misbehavior to form the training data.
paragraphs.zh: 用于终端智能体训练的标准强化学习方案，如 GRPO（Shao et al., 2024）和 DPPO（Qi et al., 2026），每次回放都从第零步开始重新进行。 这些方法的一个重要特征是它们是在线的（on-policy），即它们使用由策略自身生成的回放进行训练。 重新开始回放意味着我们无法以在线的方式纠正某个特定的错误行为，除非同一错误行为在新回放中出现并被检测到。 长时程终端智能体轨迹的高度随机性意味着，生成展示某种特定错误行为的回放将非常消耗算力。 为了更有针对性和高效地修复这些错误行为，MiRL 改为从策略表现出错误行为的既有轨迹前缀开始每组回放。 随后策略从前缀继续执行，直到回放结束。 我们为每种错误行为选取固定数量的错误行为前缀来构成训练数据。

paragraphs.en: However, a live rollout cannot start from a prefix directly. Many containers are flaky: the same command may produce different outputs depending on time, randomness, or network conditions. Such prefixes cannot reach the required state, so we discard them. The training environments are those of the remaining prefixes.

paragraphs.en: We run error profiling on 2,017 random terminal environments from TMax’s environment set, which do not overlap the evaluation benchmarks. We roll out the policy on each environment with 2 rollout seeds. We use Qwen3.8-27B ( Qwen Team, 2026b ) as the error localizer, because it is strong enough to judge terminal steps, with a reported 73.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1. We also use it as the teacher, because it belongs to the same model family as the policy, so its corrections stay close to the policy’s own distribution ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Raoof et al., 2026 ) . We use Claude Opus 5 ( Anthropic, 2026 ) as the annotator. We keep every error type that covers at least 1% of the error steps, which gives eight generalizable misbehaviors. For these eight misbehaviors, we sample 80 misbehavior prefixes each, which gives 640 prefixes. After the rerun check in Figure 3 (c), 219 prefixes remain (34%), from 189 environments.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在来自 TMax 环境集的 2,017 个随机终端环境上运行错误剖析，这些环境与评测基准不重叠。 我们在每个环境上使用 2 个 rollout 种子对策略进行 rollout。 我们使用 Qwen3.8-27B（Qwen Team, 2026b）作为错误定位器，因为它足够强大，能够判断终端步骤，其在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上的报告成绩为 73.0%。 我们还将它用作教师模型，因为它与策略属于同一模型家族，所以它的修正能保持接近策略自身的分布（Yang et al., 2026; Raoof et al., 2026）。 我们使用 Claude Opus 5（Anthropic, 2026）作为标注器。 我们保留覆盖至少 1% 错误步骤的每种错误类型，这得到了八种可泛化的不当行为。 针对这八种不当行为，我们每种各采样 80 个不当行为前缀，共得到 640 个前缀。 经过图 3 (c) 中的重跑检查后，保留了 219 个前缀（34%），来自 189 个环境。

sents.en: We run error profiling on 2,017 random terminal environments from TMax’s environment set, which do not overlap the evaluation benchmarks.
sents.zh: 我们在来自 TMax 环境集的 2,017 个随机终端环境上运行错误剖析，这些环境与评测基准不重叠。

sents.en: We roll out the policy on each environment with 2 rollout seeds.
sents.zh: 我们在每个环境上使用 2 个 rollout 种子对策略进行 rollout。

sents.en: We use Qwen3.8-27B ( Qwen Team, 2026b ) as the error localizer, because it is strong enough to judge terminal steps, with a reported 73.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
sents.zh: 我们使用 Qwen3.8-27B（Qwen Team, 2026b）作为错误定位器，因为它足够强大，能够判断终端步骤，其在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上的报告成绩为 73.0%。

sents.en: We also use it as the teacher, because it belongs to the same model family as the policy, so its corrections stay close to the policy’s own distribution ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Raoof et al., 2026 ) .
sents.zh: 我们还将它用作教师模型，因为它与策略属于同一模型家族，所以它的修正能保持接近策略自身的分布（Yang et al., 2026; Raoof et al., 2026）。

sents.en: We use Claude Opus 5 ( Anthropic, 2026 ) as the annotator.
sents.zh: 我们使用 Claude Opus 5（Anthropic, 2026）作为标注器。

sents.en: We keep every error type that covers at least 1% of the error steps, which gives eight generalizable misbehaviors.
sents.zh: 我们保留覆盖至少 1% 错误步骤的每种错误类型，这得到了八种可泛化的不当行为。

sents.en: For these eight misbehaviors, we sample 80 misbehavior prefixes each, which gives 640 prefixes.
sents.zh: 针对这八种不当行为，我们每种各采样 80 个不当行为前缀，共得到 640 个前缀。

sents.en: After the rerun check in Figure 3 (c), 219 prefixes remain (34%), from 189 environments.
sents.zh: 经过图 3 (c) 中的重跑检查后，保留了 219 个前缀（34%），来自 189 个环境。

paragraphs.en: We use Qwen3.5-4B, the same base model as TMax-4B, as the policy model. We follow the RL recipe of TMax and use their harness, except for a group size of 16 instead of 32 to control the compute budget, and a total of 160 training steps instead of 500. The behavior judge is Gemini 3.8 Flash ( Google, 2026 ) , which reads the m = 5 m=5 steps after the prefix. It returns only a binary signal, so the policy receives no text from the behavior judge to imitate. We run our experiments on 8 A100 80GB GPUs. Appendix A gives the full settings and prompts.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 Qwen3.5-4B（与 TMax-4B 相同的基座模型）作为策略模型。 我们沿用 TMax 的强化学习方案并使用其训练框架，但为了控制算力预算，将组大小从 32 改为 16，并将训练步数从 500 步减少到 160 步。 行为评判器为 Gemini 3.8 Flash（Google, 2026），它会读取前缀之后的 m=5 个步骤。 它仅返回一个二元信号，因此策略不会收到来自行为评判器的任何可供模仿的文本。 我们在 8 块 A100 80GB GPU 上运行实验。 附录 A 给出了完整的设置与提示词。

paragraphs.en: We compare MiRL with TMax-4B, the released checkpoint (step 200 of 500) trained with the full TMax recipe, which samples training environments from a pool of 14.6K. Because Terminal-Bench scores are sensitive to the evaluation hardware, we report both its published scores and our evaluation of the released checkpoint. We also train three baselines with the same configuration as MiRL, except that their 189 environments are sampled at random from the same 2,017 environments, since these baselines do not select environments by error profiling or any other method. The first, TMax-189, replicates the TMax recipe but only on 189 environments: it starts rollouts at the beginning of each task and uses the outcome reward. The other two are the closest prior methods to the two parts of MiRL. PivotRL ( Yi et al., 2026 ) also trains from selected steps of a trajectory: it samples several actions at each step, keeps the steps where these actions get different rewards, and rewards each action mainly with an LLM judge. Since each PivotRL update trains on a single step rather than on whole rollouts, matching the number of training steps is not meaningful, so we give PivotRL about the same GPU budget as TMax-189 for its full training run ( ≈ \approx 300 A100 hours). RaR ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) also rewards the process with an LLM: a judge scores the whole trajectory against a rubric generated for each environment. The original RaR uses only this rubric score, so for a fairer comparison we strengthen it with the outcome reward and call it RaR+: when the judge writes the rubric for an environment, it also sets the weights of the rubric score and the outcome reward.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 MiRL 与 TMax-4B 进行比较，后者是使用完整 TMax 配方训练的已发布检查点（500 步中的第 200 步），它从 14.6K 的环境池中采样训练环境。 由于 Terminal-Bench 的分数对评估硬件敏感，我们同时报告其已发布的分数以及我们对已发布检查点的评估结果。 我们还使用与 MiRL 相同的配置训练了三个基线，只是它们的 189 个环境是从同样的 2,017 个环境中随机采样的，因为这些基线不通过错误剖析或任何其他方法来选择环境。 第一个是 TMax-189，它复现 TMax 配方但仅在 189 个环境上进行：它从每个任务的开头开始展开，并使用结果奖励。 另外两个是与 MiRL 两个组成部分最接近的先前方法。 PivotRL（Yi et al., 2026）同样从轨迹的选定步骤进行训练：它在每个步骤采样若干动作，保留这些动作获得不同奖励的步骤，并主要用一个 LLM 裁判来对每个动作给予奖励。 由于 PivotRL 的每次更新在单个步骤上训练而非在完整展开上训练，匹配训练步数没有意义，因此我们为 PivotRL 的完整训练运行分配与 TMax-189 大致相同的 GPU 预算（≈300 A100 小时）。 RaR（Gunjal et al., 2026）同样用 LLM 对过程进行奖励：一个裁判根据为每个环境生成的评分细则对整条轨迹打分。 原始的 RaR 仅使用这一评分细则分数，因此为了更公平的比较，我们用结果奖励对其进行加强并称之为 RaR+：当裁判为某个环境撰写评分细则时，它还会设定评分细则分数与结果奖励的权重。

paragraphs.en: Error profiling on the 2,017 environments yields 12,746 error steps. Figure 4 shows their distribution over error types. The eight most frequent error types cover 52.1% of all error steps. Each appears in 6.9% (140) to 46.7% (942) of the 2,017 environments, and at least one appears in 75.4% (1,521) of them. None is specific to a particular environment, so they can be considered as generalizable misbehaviors (§ 3.1 ). Prior work observes a similar concentration: in a sample of agent trajectories, TermiGen finds that about half of the errors are verification failures, in which the agent omits a final check ( Zhu et al., 2026a ) . Our most frequent misbehavior, “Makes false claims about tests”, is also a kind of verification error.
paragraphs.zh: 对2,017个环境的错误分析共得到12,746个错误步骤。 图4展示了这些错误步骤在错误类型上的分布。 最常见的八种错误类型覆盖了全部错误步骤的52.1%。 每种错误类型出现在2,017个环境中6.9%（140个）到46.7%（942个）的环境里，且至少有一种出现在其中75.4%（1,521个）的环境中。 没有任何一种是特定环境所独有的，因此它们可被视为可泛化的不当行为（§ 3.1）。 已有工作观察到类似的集中现象：TermiGen在一份智能体轨迹样本中发现，约一半的错误是验证失败，即智能体遗漏了最终检查（Zhu et al., 2026a）。 我们最常见的错误行为「对测试作出虚假声明」也是一种验证错误。

paragraphs.en: Figure 5 shows the terminal task performance. On our evaluation hardware, both the base model and TMax-4B achieve higher scores than their published ones (e.g., 47.4% vs. 42.6% for TMax-4B on TB-Lite), so we compare all recipes with our own runs. MiRL reaches 51.8% on TB-Lite and 21.3% on TB-2.1, compared with 47.4% and 20.6% for TMax-4B on our evaluation hardware: it gains 4.4 more points on TB-Lite and matches TMax-4B on TB-2.1.
paragraphs.zh: 图5展示了最终任务性能。 在我们的评估硬件上，基础模型和TMax-4B取得的分数均高于其已公布的分数（例如，TMax-4B在TB-Lite上为47.4%对42.6%），因此我们将所有方案与我们自己运行的结果进行比较。 MiRL在TB-Lite上达到51.8%，在TB-2.1上达到21.3%，而在我们的评估硬件上TMax-4B分别为47.4%和20.6%：它在TB-Lite上多获得4.4分，在TB-2.1上与TMax-4B持平。

paragraphs.en: On 189 random environments, TMax-189 improves the base model by 10.6 points on TB-Lite, which is the smallest gain among the four recipes trained with a controlled number of environments. This indicates that a small random set is not enough for the standard recipe of RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR; Lambert et al., 2025 ). PivotRL and RaR+ improve the base model more, by 14.4 and 14.8 points on TB-Lite. MiRL outperforms the best of these baselines by 4.2 points on TB-Lite and 2.2 points on TB-2.1. The result suggests that targeting generalizable misbehaviors is an effective way to choose where rollouts start and what the judge checks.

paragraphs.en: We ablate MiRL by adding its three parts one at a time to TMax-189 (Figure 6 ). Training on the environments where the misbehaviors occur lowers the score from 43.4% to 37.4% on TB-Lite and from 17.6% to 16.5% on TB-2.1. We attribute this to the higher difficulty of these environments for the policy: the share of groups in which all rollouts fail, which give no learning signal, rises from 27.3% to 42.9%. However, environment selection is not meant to help on its own. Instead, it provides the misbehavior prefixes for the next two parts. Starting rollouts at misbehavior prefixes adds 7.9 points on TB-Lite and 1.5 points on TB-2.1. We attribute this gain to training on the steps where the policy misbehaves, even though no reward checks the misbehavior yet. The behavior reward r e r_{e} adds 6.5 points on TB-Lite and 3.3 points on TB-2.1. With r e r_{e} , the reward is stricter than the outcome reward alone: it excludes the rollouts that pass the tests but still misbehave. For example, a policy may claim success without verification. When its first attempt happens to be correct, the rollout passes and the misbehavior is not fatal; when the first attempt is wrong, the same unchecked submission makes the rollout fail. The outcome reward alone still rewards the passing rollout, so the policy may learn to repeat the misbehavior.

paragraphs.en: To verify that MiRL reduces the misbehaviors, we measure how often each policy repeats a misbehavior before and after training. paragraphs.en: A common critique of RL is that it sharpens the output distribution of the base model rather than teaching it new capabilities ( Yue et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) . In that case, RL improves pass@1, but pass@k at large k k improves little or even falls below that of the base model. We test this on TB-2.1 with the unbiased pass@k ( Chen et al., 2021 ) , using 16 runs per task. Figure (a) compares the scores. TMax-4B shows this pattern: it improves over Qwen3.5-4B at pass@1, but the base model catches up at about k = 11 k=11 and is ahead at k = 16 k=16 . In contrast, MiRL outperforms the base model at every k k up to 16 by a large margin, and reaches 39.3% at k = 16 k=16 . Figure (b) shows how often each task is solved over the 16 runs. These results suggest that error-targeted RL raises the upper bound of the model more than standard RL does. We suspect one reason is that MiRL keeps learning in a zone of proximal development. By starting rollouts at misbehavior prefixes, MiRL only needs the policy to complete the rest of each task, and the misbehavior rate at these prefixes is mostly moderate (Figure 7 ). Prior work shows that starting from partial solutions ( Li et al., 2026a ) and moderate task difficulty ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) improve both pass@1 and pass@k.

paragraphs.en: We measure data efficiency by the training resources needed to reach a given performance level, including the resources spent on error profiling and other preprocessing. We count these resources up to each recipe’s best checkpoint rather than over its full training run. Figure 8 compares MiRL and TMax-4B up to their best checkpoints. MiRL uses fewer terminal environments, and only 35% of the rollouts and 34% of the input tokens of TMax-4B. Its output tokens drop further, to 28%, because each rollout starts from a prefix, so the policy does not generate the steps of the prefix again. As a result, MiRL uses only 39% of the GPU hours of TMax-4B. Although MiRL pays a model API fee for the LLMs in error profiling and for the behavior judge in RL training, which TMax-4B does not, its total cost is still lower, at 56% of that of TMax-4B, while it scores 4.4 points higher on TB-Lite and matches it on TB-2.1. Compared with TMax-189, MiRL uses about as many rollouts and GPU hours (26.2K vs. 26.4K rollouts and 202.8 vs. 202.7 hours) but scores 8.4 points higher on TB-Lite.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we apply error-targeted learning to terminal agents. We (i) propose error profiling, which locates and corrects the error steps of a policy and groups them into error types to find its generalizable misbehaviors, (ii) introduce MiRL, an RL recipe that starts rollouts from misbehavior prefixes and rewards a rollout only if it passes the tests and avoids the misbehavior, and (iii) show that MiRL reduces the targeted misbehaviors, outperforms or matches all baselines on two benchmarks, and uses fewer training resources than TMax-4B. These results suggest that error-targeted learning can work for long-horizon terminal tasks when training targets generalizable misbehaviors where they occur.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们将错误靶向学习应用于终端智能体。 我们 (i) 提出错误剖析（error profiling），其定位并纠正策略的错误步骤，并将它们归入错误类型以发现其可泛化的不当行为；(ii) 引入 MiRL，一种强化学习方法，它从不当行为前缀开始展开（rollout），并且仅当展开通过测试并避免了不当行为时才给予奖励；(iii) 表明 MiRL 减少了被针对的不当行为，在两个基准上优于或持平所有基线方法，并且比 TMax-4B 使用更少的训练资源。 这些结果表明，当训练以不当行为发生之处针对可泛化的不当行为时，错误靶向学习可以用于长时程终端任务。

paragraphs.en: First, we train and evaluate our method with only one model backbone, so it remains unclear how well the gains generalize to other model choices. Second, due to the compute budget, we train each recipe once and report the standard error over 3 evaluation runs, which does not capture the variance across training runs. Third, error profiling relies on external LLMs, including commercial ones, and the rerun check discards prefixes from non-deterministic environments, which may bias the training data. Finally, for reward design, we mainly try the conjunction of the two rewards and have not explored other ways to combine them.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，我们仅使用一个模型骨干来训练和评估我们的方法，因此这些收益能否泛化到其他模型选择仍不明确。 其次，由于算力预算限制，我们对每个配方只训练一次，并报告 3 次评估运行的标准误差，这无法刻画训练运行之间的方差。 第三，错误分析依赖外部大语言模型，包括商业模型，且重跑检查会丢弃来自非确定性环境的前缀，这可能会使训练数据产生偏差。 最后，在奖励设计方面，我们主要尝试了两种奖励的组合使用，尚未探索其他结合方式。

paragraphs.en: We count the training resources of each recipe up to its best checkpoint rather than over its full training run, which is fairer to recipes that train longer than needed; for example, the released TMax-4B checkpoint is from step 200 of 500, as stated on its model card. We also count the resources of all preprocessing stages, such as error profiling for MiRL, step profiling for PivotRL, and rubric writing for RaR+. Most values are measured from our logs; below we explain the values that are not.

paragraphs.en: The TMax paper reports the training settings and curves for TMax-4B, but not the total number of rollouts, tokens, or GPU hours. We estimate these totals from the reported settings and curves. The number of rollouts is S ​ B ​ G / ( 1 − d ) SBG/(1-d) , where S = 200 S=200 steps, B = 8 B=8 environments per step, G = 32 G=32 rollouts per environment, and d d is the share of dead groups, which are resampled. We derive d = 32.5 % d=32.5\% from Figure 11 in the TMax paper ( Ivison et al., 2026 ) , which counts the groups in which all rollouts fail; TMax notes that groups in which all rollouts pass are rare and does not plot them, so we count them as zero. This gives 75.9K rollouts and S ​ B / ( 1 − d ) = 2,370 SB/(1-d)=2{,}370 environments. We estimate its tokens and GPU hours from the tokens per step, steps per rollout, and throughput of our TMax-189 run, except for the output tokens per step, which come from Figure 6 in the TMax paper.

paragraphs.en: We convert the tokens of the policy into dollars at the Tinker prices in Table 4 , taking the uncached share of the input tokens as two divided by the average number of steps per rollout, and add the model API fee. This prices the policy as a service billed per token rather than as a rented GPU cluster, so we report the GPU hours separately and do not add them to the total cost.
paragraphs.zh: 我们按照表4中的Tinker价格将策略的token转换为美元，其中未缓存输入token的占比取为2除以每次rollout的平均步数，并加上模型API费用。 这种定价方式是将策略视为按token计费的服务，而非租用的GPU集群，因此我们单独报告GPU小时数，不将其计入总成本。
